feedback: If a dinosaur is placed in the wrong period, show its correct period and name a well-known companion that shared it, so the period gains concrete inhabitants.

When the Stegosaurus–T. rex gap is marked, confirm it is about 80 million years: because they lived in different periods separated by that span, the two never coexisted — and note that this gap is even larger than the ~66 million years from T. rex to today.
If a learner assumes all dinosaurs could meet, lay the three periods out and show Stegosaurus and T. rex tens of millions of years apart: different dinosaurs, different eras.
If a learner accepts different periods but still imagines them short enough to overlap, make the vastness concrete with the gap comparison before accepting the answer.
activities.intendedInsight: The Age of Dinosaurs was not one crowded scene; different casts of dinosaurs lived and vanished across tens of millions of years, and the gap between two famous dinosaurs can exceed the gap between the later one and us.
learnerActions: Set up three slots left to right in order: Triassic, then Jurassic, then Cretaceous.

Sort a set of famous dinosaurs into the correct period: e.g. early dinosaurs/Plateosaurus into the Triassic; Stegosaurus, Brachiosaurus and Allosaurus into the Jurassic; T. rex, Triceratops and Velociraptor into the Cretaceous.

After placing Stegosaurus (Jurassic) and T. rex (Cretaceous), mark the distance between them on the timeline, then compare it to the distance from T. rex to a 'you, today' marker placed at the end of the line.
State in your own words whether Stegosaurus and T. rex could ever have met, and why.
activities.title: Build the timeline and sort the dinosaurs

feedback: A full response orders the periods, assigns species, and reasons that dinosaurs living tens of millions of years apart, like Stegosaurus and T. rex, never met, citing the Stegosaurus/T. rex gap.
A partial response orders the periods and assigns a dinosaur but still imagines overlap; respond by re-marking the gap magnitude.

A correct model answer: 'No. Stegosaurus lived in the Jurassic and T. rex in the Cretaceous — about 80 million years apart — so they never met; different dinosaurs lived in different periods, each spanning enormous stretches of time.'
activities.intendedInsight: Chronological order of the periods plus the magnitude of the gaps together explain why dinosaurs separated by tens of millions of years, such as Stegosaurus and T. rex or a Triassic and a Cretaceous dinosaur, never coexisted.
learnerActions: Answer true/false: there is more time between Stegosaurus and T. rex than between T. rex and you — and explain how you know.
Answer: which lived longer ago, Stegosaurus or T. rex, and how can you tell from the timeline?
Answer: could a Triassic dinosaur ever have met a Cretaceous one? Explain why or why not.
Respond to the prompt: 'Stegosaurus and T. rex must have fought because they were both dinosaurs living at the same time.' Say whether this is right and explain.
Explain in a sentence or two why the 'Age of Dinosaurs' (over ~150 million years) was an enormous span, not a single scene.
activities.title: Explain and probe deep time
